transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, I just don't care about anything anymore. It's like a switch flipped. I used to love my art classes, you know? I was working on this big charcoal piece, a portrait of my neighbor's dog. It was a Golden Retriever, really sweet, always trying to eat the mail carrier's shoes. I think they bought him special chew toys just to distract him, but he preferred the leather. Anyway, I haven't touched the charcoal in weeks. I don't care about board-game nights with my friends, or hiking... I used to go up to the ridge every weekend. The air is so crisp up there, especially in October when the leaves turn. But now I just sit in my room. Even the thought of getting back to my soccer team... it just feels pointless. I just sit there while everything slips away. It's like watching a movie I don't even want to be in.
Have you been having thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?

Yeah... I just... I keep having these thoughts that I don't want to wake up anymore. I just want to stay under the covers. My friend got me this really heavy duvet, actually. She found it at one of those discount home stores, she’s always looking for a good deal. She has this whole system with the clearance racks in the back of the store... she says you always have to check the back aisles first before you look at anything else. She found this amazing glass vase there once, it looked just like Murano glass, which is made in Italy, near Venice. I've always wanted to go to Venice before it sinks. They say the water levels keep rising every year and it's just ruining the foundations of those beautiful old buildings, all that history just washing away... 

Anyway, she came over to my apartment to check on me because I wasn't answering my phone. She has a spare key. And when she found me... I didn't even realize I was doing it, but I had been saying out loud that I couldn't keep living like this. I was just sitting there talking to the empty room.
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed and lost interest in things like this for at least a couple of weeks?

No, I... I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days, sure, but nothing like this. It's just so heavy now. Speaking of heavy, my brother used to lift weights. Like, seriously heavy weights. He was in this powerlifting competition down in Florida a few years ago. Florida is so weird, right? Like, the humidity just hits you the second you step off the plane. I went to Orlando once when I was a kid. We went to that theme park with the big golf ball thing. Epcot! That's it. We rode this ride that smelled like oranges. They pump the smell in, which is kind of genius when you think about it. The psychology of scent is fascinating. Like how lavender is supposed to make you sleepy. I bought this lavender essential oil rollerball thing at a farmer's market, but the lady who sold it to me was so pushy. She kept trying to sell me on these crystals too. Rose quartz for love, amethyst for anxiety... I don't know if I buy into all that. But anyway, no, I haven't really felt this bad before.
Did this start after something stressful happened in your life?

Well, yeah, it did, actually. It started right after my divorce. That was... gosh, it's been about a year and 11 months now since it all started. The divorce was just a nightmare. We had to split everything, even the vinyl collection. My ex-husband, he was obsessed with collecting records. He had this original pressing of Fleetwood Mac's Rumours, which is a great album, don't get me wrong. "Dreams" is such a good song. Did you know Stevie Nicks wrote that in like, 10 minutes? She just sat on a bed with a keyboard and it came to her. I wish I could do that. I tried playing the piano when I was little, but my teacher, Mrs. Gable, she had these really long fingernails that would click on the keys. Click, click, click. It drove me absolutely crazy. She always smelled like mothballs, too. You know that smell? It just gets into everything. My grandmother used to put mothballs in all her closets to protect her winter coats. She had this beautiful mink coat she bought in the 60s. People don't really wear real fur anymore, though, do they? It's kind of frowned upon now. But yeah, the divorce was really stressful, and this whole feeling just started right after that.
Since the divorce, have you felt this way continuously the whole time?

Well, not the whole time, no. At first it was just... bad days here and there. But then around the following summer, it just became constant. It's been like this for about a year and four months now. Summer is usually my favorite time of year, too. I love when the fireflies come out. We used to catch them in mason jars when we were kids, my brother and I. We'd poke holes in the lid so they could breathe, and put grass in the bottom. My mom would always make us let them go before bed, though. She said it was cruel to keep them locked up. She was always really big on animal rights. She used to volunteer at this shelter on weekends, walking the dogs. There was this one dog, a pitbull mix named Buster, who was just the sweetest thing. People are so scared of pitbulls, but it's really all about how you raise them, you know? It's like kids. If you raise a kid in a loving environment, they usually turn out okay. But if they're constantly yelled at... well, that's a whole different story. But yeah, the heavy, constant feeling... it's been about a year and four months of just... not being able to shake it.
Since this got bad, has your appetite changed?

Yeah, I just... I go most of the day without eating anything now. It's like everything just tastes like cardboard to me, so I don't even bother. I've lost a lot of weight because of it. My jeans have gotten so loose that I actually have to knot the waistband just to keep them from falling down. I bought these jeans at the mall a couple of years ago... you know, back when the mall actually had good stores. Now it's just half empty. It's so sad what's happening to indoor shopping malls, isn't it? They used to be the place to go when I was a teenager. We'd hang out at the food court for hours. Oh, the food court... they had this amazing pretzel place. Auntie Anne's, I think? Or maybe it was Wetzel's Pretzels. I always got the cinnamon sugar one. Cinnamon is such a strong spice. I read somewhere once that if you smell cinnamon, it can actually boost your memory and cognitive function. I should probably carry some cinnamon sticks around with me, honestly. I saw them at the craft store around the holidays. People use them to make those scented pinecone wreaths. My aunt makes those every December... But yeah, I just don't really have an appetite anymore.
Have other people noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking much more slowly than usual?

Well, my sister mentioned something the other day. She said I was moving like I was underwater. And she's right, sometimes I move so slowly that just trying to make a pot of coffee feels like I'm trying to lift wet cement. It takes forever. Speaking of coffee, I used to go to this little cafe down the street, The Daily Grind. They had the best roast. It wasn't that bitter, burnt stuff you get at the big chains, you know? The owner, Marcus, he roasted the beans himself in the back. He was always talking about the acidity levels and where the beans came from... Ethiopia, Colombia, Costa Rica. Costa Rica is supposed to be beautiful. I've always wanted to go there and see the rainforests. They have those sloths that just hang upside down in the trees all day. They move so slowly, kind of like I do sometimes. But then, on other days, I'm the complete opposite. I'll just pace back and forth, from the kitchen to the living room window, over and over until my legs actually ache. I just can't stop moving. It's like I have all this nervous energy and nowhere to put it. I wear socks when I pace because the hardwood floors get so cold. I have these fuzzy socks with penguins on them. Penguins are fascinating, how they huddle together in the freezing cold to stay warm. The males are the ones who sit on the eggs, you know. They just stand there in the blizzard for months. I can't even imagine being that cold for that long. But yeah, people have definitely noticed that my movements are just... all over the place lately.
When you were talking out loud to the empty room, did you hear a voice speaking back to you?

Yeah, I... I do. It's a woman's voice. She usually comes from the corner of my bedroom, and she tells me that I ruined everything and that I just need to stay inside. It's so loud, like she's standing right next to my bed. My bed is right by the window, actually. I put it there so I could get the morning light, but the blinds are broken. One of the slats snapped when I was trying to dust them. Dusting is such a pointless chore, isn't it? You wipe it away and two days later it's just back again. Dust is mostly dead skin cells, which is kind of gross if you think about it too much. I used to buy those Swiffer dusters, the fluffy ones? They trap the dust instead of just pushing it around. They're made of some kind of microfiber. Microfiber is great for cleaning glasses, too. I don't wear glasses, but my ex-husband did. He was always losing them. He'd leave them on the bathroom counter, or on top of the fridge for some reason. The fridge we had was one of those stainless steel ones that shows every single fingerprint. You're supposed to use special polish for it, but honestly, baby oil works just as well. I read that in a magazine in a waiting room once. Magazines are all just ads now, anyway. But yeah, the voice... it's just this woman, clear as day, telling me I ruined everything.
Does the woman’s voice ever say anything other than blaming you or telling you to stay inside?

No, it's just... it's just that same stuff. She just says I ruined everything and that I need to stay inside. It's always from that same corner of the room, too. It's so clear, it really does sound like someone is just standing right there by my bed. I wish I could move my bed, honestly, but it's too heavy. It's a solid oak frame. My parents bought it for me when I got my first apartment. Oak is supposed to last forever, right? It's a hardwood. They use oak to make wine barrels, I think. Or maybe that's cedar. No, cedar is for closets to keep the moths away. Moths are so creepy, the way they just flutter around the porch light. They're like ugly butterflies. Butterflies are beautiful, though. I went to a butterfly conservatory once on a field trip in middle school. It was so humid in there, like walking into a greenhouse. They had all these tropical plants and the butterflies would just land right on your shoulder if you stood still enough. I tried to stand as still as a statue, but my nose started itching and I had to move, and they all flew away. It's hard to stay perfectly still. But anyway, no, the voice doesn't really say anything else. Just that I ruined everything and to stay inside.
Before this depression began, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I don't think so... I can't really remember another time in my life where it was like this. Two weeks is such a specific amount of time, though. A fortnight. I always thought that was such a funny, old-fashioned word. You really only see it in those old Victorian novels. I tried to read Great Expectations when I was taking some classes at the community college. My professor was this older guy, Mr. Henderson, and he always wore those tweed jackets with the leather patches on the elbows. I always wondered why they put patches just on the elbows. I guess if you lean on a desk all day, the fabric wears out. I hate sitting at desks, they make my back hurt. I actually bought one of those standing desks a few years ago because I read an article in a waiting room saying that sitting is the new smoking. Smoking is so awful. My aunt used to smoke like a chimney, and her whole house just smelled like stale ash and peppermint. She always kept peppermint candies in this little crystal bowl on her coffee table to try and hide the smell on her breath, but it never worked. They were those ones with the red and white swirls, wrapped in that clear plastic that makes so much noise when you try to open it. But... wait, what did you ask me? About being depressed before this? Yeah, no, I don't think I have.

But yeah, the voice... it's just this woman, clear as day, telling me I ruined everything.

inference.note: New clear auditory hallucinations with depressive content adds psychotic depression (F32.3). Given episode duration >1 year, recurrent severe depressive disorder with psychotic symptoms (F33.3) remains a differential until prior episodes are clarified, though history so far suggests first episode.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the hallucinated voice is mood-congruent, which helps distinguish major depressive disorder with psychotic features from nonpsychotic depression or adjustment/anxiety disorders.
doctor.question: Does the woman’s voice ever say anything other than blaming you or telling you to stay inside?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: I hear a woman’s voice from the corner of my room saying I ruined everything and should stay inside, and it sounds as clear as someone standing right next to my bed.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking for more details about the content of the auditory hallucination (the woman's voice).

patient.answer: No, it's just... it's just that same stuff. She just says I ruined everything and that I need to stay inside. It's always from that same corner of the room, too. It's so clear, it really does sound like someone is just standing right there by my bed. I wish I could move my bed, honestly, but it's too heavy. It's a solid oak frame. My parents bought it for me when I got my first apartment. Oak is supposed to last forever, right? It's a hardwood. They use oak to make wine barrels, I think. Or maybe that's cedar. No, cedar is for closets to keep the moths away. Moths are so creepy, the way they just flutter around the porch light. They're like ugly butterflies. Butterflies are beautiful, though. I went to a butterfly conservatory once on a field trip in middle school. It was so humid in there, like walking into a greenhouse. They had all these tropical plants and the butterflies would just land right on your shoulder if you stood still enough. I tried to stand as still as a statue, but my nose started itching and I had to move, and they all flew away. It's hard to stay perfectly still. But anyway, no, the voice doesn't really say anything else. Just that I ruined everything and to stay inside.

inference.note: Auditory hallucinations with mood-congruent guilt/persecutory content during a severe depressive episode support psychotic depression. History suggests a single prolonged episode after divorce, but because total duration is near 2 years and chronology could imply persistence/recurrence, keep both single-episode and recurrent severe depression with psychotic symptoms; nonpsychotic depression, adjustment disorder, and mixed anxiety/depression are no longer adequate.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there was any prior major depressive episode before the current illness, to distinguish a single episode major depressive disorder with psychotic features from recurrent major depressive disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Before this depression began, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a history of depressive episodes prior to the current illness, which is not covered in the symptom profile.

patient.answer: I don't think so... I can't really remember another time in my life where it was like this. Two weeks is such a specific amount of time, though. A fortnight. I always thought that was such a funny, old-fashioned word. You really only see it in those old Victorian novels. I tried to read Great Expectations when I was taking some classes at the community college. My professor was this older guy, Mr. Henderson, and he always wore those tweed jackets with the leather patches on the elbows. I always wondered why they put patches just on the elbows. I guess if you lean on a desk all day, the fabric wears out. I hate sitting at desks, they make my back hurt. I actually bought one of those standing desks a few years ago because I read an article in a waiting room saying that sitting is the new smoking. Smoking is so awful. My aunt used to smoke like a chimney, and her whole house just smelled like stale ash and peppermint. She always kept peppermint candies in this little crystal bowl on her coffee table to try and hide the smell on her breath, but it never worked. They were those ones with the red and white swirls, wrapped in that clear plastic that makes so much noise when you try to open it. But... wait, what did you ask me? About being depressed before this? Yeah, no, I don't think I have.

inference.note: No history of prior depressive episodes despite repeated probing, which rules against recurrent depressive disorder with psychotic symptoms (F33.3). Current picture remains a single severe depressive episode with mood-congruent auditory hallucinations.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient describes a first depressive episode with persistent depressed mood/anhedonia, suicidal thoughts, appetite/weight loss, psychomotor change, and mood-congruent auditory hallucinations. Symptoms became continuously severe for over a year, with no prior depressive episodes reported, supporting a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms rather than recurrent depressive disorder. Although onset followed divorce, the syndrome exceeds adjustment disorder in severity, duration, and presence of psychotic symptoms.
